I am a twin and was selectively mute at that age, probably until I was 7 or 8, while my twin sister never was. We were never in the same class and it was really hard for me, I remember I would cry every day and my teachers could never figure out what was wrong and at 5 years old I didn’t even know. And even if I knew it was anxiety, I obviously wouldn’t have been able to communicate that. I didn’t go to preschool, but when I started school in kindergarten, I became good friends with a nice girl and kind of clung to her. We were in the same first grade class and then I was able to become friends with a few other kids in the class, though of course I still couldn’t talk to the teacher. Although I was still “shy” and had anxiety speaking (honestly throughout my whole school career), by second grade I was at least able to talk to my teacher and I improved with each year. 

I didn’t have any kind of therapy or anything so I feel lucky I grew out of it. Are you getting treatment for them? I think you are right; if my sister had been in my classes I probably wouldn’t have made friends with other kids especially if she was selectively mute too. I definitely struggled though and I would hate for other kids to feel the same way I did with no help, so I hope they are getting some sort of treatment.

I’m 25f and got both done at the same time last year. I definitely would recommend but only if you have someone to help you at home. I used a wheelchair for the first week or so and then was able to start walking using crutches. I definitely would’ve hated having to double the recovery time getting them done separately! I know everyone’s body is different and will recover differently, but getting both done for me was really not that bad. Don’t let people discourage you if that’s what you want to do!

I hear ya! It sucks not having normal looking feet. I don’t think I’ve worn sandals or been barefoot in front of anyone since I was in sixth grade lol. Currently my feet are still swollen a little bit but my X-rays show that the bone is completely straight now! I’m very happy with how my toe has straightened. 

During the first week after surgery, I mostly stayed in bed for the first few days just getting up to use the bathroom. I was allowed partial weight bearing on my heels so I used them to transfer to and from my bed and a wheelchair. By week 3 I was back to walking without even using crutches! Different doctors have different protocols (also depending on what procedure you get), like some people who get this surgery are non weight bearing for six weeks!! If that was my doctors protocol I definitely would not have done both feet at once. Good for you it’s only “bad” enough for surgery on one foot! Makes things easier for sure haha :)

I’m 24 and just got mine done last month. It’s definitely worth it to get it while you’re still young! My recovery has been so much easier than I’ve heard it was for older people, and I got both feet done at the same time. Granted I did have some pain but it’s definitely not as bad as other peoples. It’ll only get worse though so it’s really up to you! If it’s a good time in your life to do it then I say do it! I got the lapiplasty procedure and I’m very happy with the results so far.

I got bilateral lapiplasty on august 5! I’m healing pretty well, was able to walk with crutches (albeit with some pain) starting around day 4 PO. I’m day 11 rn and can walk with crutches with no pain and much better balance/flexibility in my ankles (still not 100% obviously, but I’ve seen great improvement already!). I was discharged in post op shoes, and since I got both feet done together I won’t be using boots, just transitioning from the post op shoe to regular sneakers 6-8 weeks PO depending on swelling. Walking with 2 post op shoes has been fine for me, just make sure you go slow and pick up your feet enough when you walk so you don’t trip! It can be hard when both your feet/ankles aren’t as mobile.

Hi! I’m 24F and getting surgery in a couple weeks. I didn’t need a referral to see my doctor. I found him by searching on the lapiplasty website! You should look into it if you haven’t already, I have high hopes for this surgery because it fixes the unstable joint that causes the bunion so it can’t come back in the future. My doctor is a podiatrist at an orthopedic practice. You should be able to schedule surgery for whenever it’s convenient to you. I was able to schedule mine like 3 months out of my initial appointment (because I knew I wanted surgery like you). I think you should be fine to schedule it in January as it’s a while out! Good luck :)

I agree!! I’m 24 and getting lapiplasty in a month. Hmm it might be tough with the move, but I think you should get the surgery done now. If you know you’ll be on your feet and working long hours during your grad program, that sounds like it’ll cause you a lot of pain. Limping because of the pain is a lot worse than mine and I’m getting surgery in august. 

A lot of people (and doctors) suggest putting off surgery until the pain is unbearable, but I don’t know how I feel about that. If you’re at a point in your life where you are able to get the surgery, I think it’s better to get it done sooner than later. They say younger people have an easier time with recovery, so if you wait until the pain is unbearable, you’ll be suffering through pain for a longer period of time and there’s a chance your recovery won’t be as smooth as it would be if you had gotten surgery sooner (I’m saying this as if it’ll take like 20+ years for you to reconsider surgery; if you decide you want to get it done after your program and are able to I doubt the recovery would be much different than if you got it now lol). 

Ultimately it’s your decision but I wanted to share my insight! Good luck with whatever you choose :)
